def test_article_update_changes_fields_and_preserves_slug():
    base_url = "http://localhost:3000/api"

    # Generate unique test data to avoid collisions
    unique_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
    username = f"testuser_{unique_id}"
    email = f"{username}@example.com"
    password = "password123"

    register_data = {
        "user": {
            "username": username,
            "email": email,
            "password": password
        }
    }
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/users", json=register_data)
    assert resp.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201, got {resp.status_code}, response: {resp.text}"
    user_data = resp.json()["user"]
    token = user_data["token"]
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Token {token}"}

    # 2. Create an article
    article_title = f"Test Article {unique_id}"
    article_description = "Initial description"
    article_body = "Initial body content"
    create_data = {
        "article": {
            "title": article_title,
            "description": article_description,
            "body": article_body,
            "tagList": ["test", "pytest"]
        }
    }
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/articles", json=create_data, headers=headers)
    assert resp.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201, got {resp.status_code}, response: {resp.text}"
    article = resp.json()
    original_slug = article["slug"]

def test_update_password_superuser_self():
    base_url = "http://localhost:8000"
    email = "admin@example.com"
    original_password = "password123"
    new_password = "newpassword123"

    # Step 1: Login with original credentials to obtain token
    login_url = f"{base_url}/api/v1/login/access-token"
    login_data = {"username": email, "password": original_password}
    resp = requests.post(login_url, data=login_data)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {resp.text}"
    token1 = resp.json()["access_token"]
    assert token1, "No access token received"

    # Step 2: Update password to new password
    update_url = f"{base_url}/api/v1/users/me/password"
    headers1 = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token1}"}
    update_payload = {
        "current_password": original_password,
        "new_password": new_password
    }
    resp = requests.patch(update_url, json=update_payload, headers=headers1)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Update failed: {resp.text}"
    resp_json = resp.json()
    assert "message" in resp_json
    assert resp_json["message"] == "Password updated successfully"

    # Step 3: Verify login with the new password
    login_data_new = {"username": email, "password": new_password}
    resp = requests.post(login_url, data=login_data_new)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login with new password failed: {resp.text}"
    token2 = resp.json()["access_token"]
    assert token2, "No access token received"

    # Step 4: Revert password back to original
    headers2 = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token2}"}
    revert_payload = {
        "current_password": new_password,
        "new_password": original_password
    }
    resp = requests.patch(update_url, json=revert_payload, headers=headers2)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Revert failed: {resp.text}"
    resp_json = resp.json()

    # Step 5: Verify login with original password again
    resp = requests.post(login_url, data=login_data)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login with original password after revert failed: {resp.text}"
    token3 = resp.json()["access_token"]

    access_token = login_json["access_token"]

    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"}

    # 2) Update superuser's own password (current -> new)
    update_response = requests.patch(
        update_password_url,
        json={
            "current_password": original_password,
            "new_password": new_password
        },
        headers=headers
    )
    assert update_response.status_code == 200, f"Password update failed: {update_response.status_code} - {update_response.text}"
    update_json = update_response.json()
    assert isinstance(update_json, dict), "Password update response is not JSON"

        data={

            "username": admin_email,
            "password": new_password
        }

        f"Login with new password failed: {login_with_new_response.status_code} - {login_with_new_response.text}"

    assert isinstance(login_with_new_json, dict), "Login with new password response is not JSON"
    assert "access_token" in login_with_new_json, "Login with new password missing access_token"

    # 4) Revert the password back to the original (new -> current/original)
    revert_response = requests.patch(
        update_password_url,
        json={
            "current_password": new_password,

    revert_json = revert_response.json()

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"

def _assert_uuid4(value: str):
    try:
        uuid_obj = uuid.UUID(value)
    except Exception:
        pytest.fail(f"Value is not a valid UUID: {value}")
    assert str(uuid_obj) == value

def _extract_token_from_html(html: str) -> str:
    # Try multiple common patterns to extract a reset token from HTML content.
    # 1) token=<token> in href or query param
    m = re.search(r"[?&]token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-\.%]+)", html)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    # 2) /reset-password/<token> style
    m = re.search(r"/reset-password/?[\"'/>]?([A-Za-z0-9_\-\.%]+)", html)
    if m:
        # The group might include characters that are actually part of surrounding markup,
        # attempt to strip trailing punctuation.
        token = m.group(1).rstrip('"\'>)')
        return token
    # 3) JSON-ish "token":"..."
    m = re.search(r"\"token\"\s*:\s*\"([A-Za-z0-9_\-\.%]+)\"", html)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    # 4) any long base64-like token sequence (fallback, but still conservative)
    m = re.search(r"([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,})", html)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    return ""

    token_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/login/access-token"
    login_data = {
        "username": "admin@example.com",
        "password": "password123"
    }
    resp = requests.post(token_url, data=login_data, timeout=10)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 from login, got {resp.status_code}, body: {resp.text}"
    login_json = resp.json()
    # Strict checks for token structure and types
    assert isinstance(login_json, dict), "Login response is not a JSON object"
    assert "access_token" in login_json, f"Login response missing 'access_token': {login_json}"
    assert isinstance(login_json["access_token"], str) and login_json["access_token"], "access_token must be a non-empty string"
    # token_type may be present and typically 'bearer'
    assert "token_type" in login_json, f"Login response missing 'token_type': {login_json}"
    assert isinstance(login_json["token_type"], str), "token_type must be a string"
    assert login_json["token_type"].lower() == "bearer", f"Expected token_type 'bearer', got '{login_json['token_type']}'"

    access_token = login_json["access_token"]

    # Step 2: Attempt to create the same admin user via protected create-user endpoint
    create_user_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    user_payload = {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "password": "password123"
    }
    resp2 = requests.post(create_user_url, json=user_payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)

    # The requirement: duplicate creation should be rejected.
    # Expect a 400 Bad Request with a JSON body containing a precise "detail" message.
    assert resp2.status_code == 400, (
        f"Expected status code 400 for duplicate user creation, got {resp2.status_code}. Response body: {resp2.text}"

    # Response must be JSON with exact structure {"detail": "..."}

    assert "detail" in body, f"Expected 'detail' key in response body, got: {body}"
    assert isinstance(body["detail"], str), f"'detail' must be a string, got: {type(body['detail'])}"

    # Exact message asserted (strict). This mirrors the expected server behavior for duplicate user creation.

import requests
import pytest

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000/api"


def register_user(username: str, email: str, password: str) -> dict:
    resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/users",
        json={"user": {"username": username, "email": email, "password": password}},
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 201, f"User registration failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    return resp.json()


def login_user(email: str, password: str) -> str:
    resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/users/login",
        json={"user": {"email": email, "password": password}},
    )
    assert resp.status_code in (200, 201), f"Login failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    data = resp.json()
    assert "user" in data and "token" in data["user"], "Token missing in login response"
    return data["user"]["token"]


def get_profile(username: str, token: str) -> dict:
    resp = requests.get(
        f"{BASE_URL}/profiles/{username}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Token {token}"},
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Get profile failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    json_data = resp.json()
    assert "profile" in json_data, "Missing 'profile' key in response"
    return json_data["profile"]


def follow_user(username: str, token: str) -> dict:
    resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/profiles/{username}/follow",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Token {token}"},
    )
    assert resp.status_code in (200, 201), f"Follow failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    json_data = resp.json()
    assert "profile" in json_data, "Missing 'profile' key in follow response"
    return json_data["profile"]


def unfollow_user(username: str, token: str) -> requests.Response:
    return requests.delete(
        f"{BASE_URL}/profiles/{username}/follow",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Token {token}"},
    )


def test_follow_unfollow_flow():
    # Create users
    user1 = {"username": "unfollower1", "email": "unfollower1@test.com", "password": "pass123"}
    user2 = {"username": "unfollowee1", "email": "unfollowee1@test.com", "password": "pass123"}

    register_user(**user1)
    register_user(**user2)

    # Login users
    token1 = login_user(user1["email"], user1["password"])
    token2 = login_user(user2["email"], user2["password"])

    # User1 follows User2
    profile_after_follow = follow_user(user2["username"], token1)
    assert profile_after_follow["username"] == user2["username"]
    assert isinstance(profile_after_follow["following"], bool)
    assert profile_after_follow["following"] is True

    # Verify following via GET profile (auth optional but we use token1)
    profile_via_get = get_profile(user2["username"], token1)
    assert profile_via_get["following"] is True

    # User1 unfollows User2
    resp_unfollow = unfollow_user(user2["username"], token1)
    assert resp_unfollow.status_code == 200, f"Unfollow failed: {resp_unfollow.status_code} {resp_unfollow.text}"
    json_unfollow = resp_unfollow.json()
    assert "profile" in json_unfollow, "Missing 'profile' key in unfollow response"
    profile_after_unfollow = json_unfollow["profile"]
    assert profile_after_unfollow["username"] == user2["username"]
    assert isinstance(profile_after_unfollow["following"], bool)
    assert profile_after_unfollow["following"] is False

    # GET profile again to ensure following is false
    profile_after_unfollow_get = get_profile(user2["username"], token1)
    assert profile_after_unfollow_get["following"] is False

    # Attempt to unfollow self - should return 400
    resp_self_unfollow = unfollow_user(user1["username"], token1)
    assert resp_self_unfollow.status_code == 400, (
        f"Self-unfollow expected 400 but got {resp_self_unfollow.status_code}"
    )

from datetime import datetime

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000/api"


def _parse_iso_datetime(s: str) -> datetime:
    # Accept datetimes like "2023-01-01T12:00:00.000Z" or with offset
    if s is None or not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError("Invalid datetime string")
    if s.endswith("Z"):
        s = s[:-1] + "+00:00"
    return datetime.fromisoformat(s)


def test_article_timestamps_update():
    # 1) Register a new user
    user_payload = {
        "user": {
            "username": "timestampuser1",
            "email": "timestampuser1@test.com",
            "password": "pass123"
        }
    }
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/users", json=user_payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201 Created for user registration, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    resp = r.json()
    assert isinstance(resp, dict), "User creation response is not a JSON object"
    assert "user" in resp and isinstance(resp["user"], dict), "User creation response missing 'user' object"
    user_obj = resp["user"]
    assert user_obj.get("username") == "timestampuser1", "Returned username does not match"
    assert user_obj.get("email") == "timestampuser1@test.com", "Returned email does not match"
    token = user_obj.get("token")
    assert isinstance(token, str) and token.strip(), "Token missing or invalid in user creation response"

    auth_headers = {"Authorization": f"Token {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

    # 2) Create an article
    article_payload = {
        "article": {
            "title": "Timestamp Test Article",
            "description": "Testing timestamps",
            "body": "Body for timestamp test"
        }
    }
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/articles", json=article_payload, headers=auth_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201 Created for article creation, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    created_article = r.json()
    assert isinstance(created_article, dict), "Article creation response is not a JSON object"

    # According to the OpenAPI spec, POST /articles returns an UnwrappedArticleResponse (article fields at top level)
    # Validate presence and types of expected fields
    for field in ("slug", "title", "created", "updated"):
        assert field in created_article, f"Field '{field}' missing in article creation response"
    assert created_article["title"] == "Timestamp Test Article", "Article title does not match the request"

    slug = created_article["slug"]
    assert isinstance(slug, str) and slug.strip(), "Invalid slug returned"

    created_ts_orig = created_article["created"]
    updated_ts_orig = created_article["updated"]
    assert isinstance(created_ts_orig, str) and isinstance(updated_ts_orig, str), "Timestamps must be strings"

    # Parse datetimes to ensure they are valid ISO datetimes
    created_dt_orig = _parse_iso_datetime(created_ts_orig)
    updated_dt_orig = _parse_iso_datetime(updated_ts_orig)
    # The updated timestamp should be equal or after created at creation time
    assert updated_dt_orig >= created_dt_orig, "Article 'updated' timestamp is earlier than 'created' on creation"

    # 3) Wait briefly to ensure timestamp difference on update
    time.sleep(1.5)

    # 4) Update article title via PUT
    update_payload = {"article": {"title": "Updated Timestamp Article"}}
    r = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/articles/{slug}", json=update_payload, headers=auth_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 OK for article update, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    put_resp = r.json()
    assert isinstance(put_resp, dict), "PUT /articles response is not a JSON object"
    assert "article" in put_resp and isinstance(put_resp["article"], dict), "PUT response missing 'article' wrapper"
    updated_article_wrapper = put_resp["article"]
    assert updated_article_wrapper.get("title") == "Updated Timestamp Article", "Article title was not updated in PUT response"
    # Validate returned timestamps in PUT response
    assert "created" in updated_article_wrapper and "updated" in updated_article_wrapper, "Timestamps missing in PUT response"
    created_ts_after_put = updated_article_wrapper["created"]
    updated_ts_after_put = updated_article_wrapper["updated"]
    assert created_ts_after_put == created_ts_orig, "Created timestamp changed after update in PUT response (should be unchanged)"

    # 5) GET the article and verify timestamps
    r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/articles/{slug}")
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 OK for GET article, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    get_resp = r.json()
    assert isinstance(get_resp, dict), "GET /articles response is not a JSON object"
    assert "article" in get_resp and isinstance(get_resp["article"], dict), "GET response missing 'article' wrapper"
    article_after_get = get_resp["article"]

    assert created_ts_get == created_ts_orig, (
        f"'created' timestamp changed after update. original={created_ts_orig}, after_get={created_ts_get}"
    )

    # Verify updated timestamp is different and newer than the original updated timestamp
    assert updated_ts_get != updated_ts_orig, (
        f"'updated' timestamp did not change after update. original={updated_ts_orig}, after_get={updated_ts_get}"
    )

    updated_dt_get = _parse_iso_datetime(updated_ts_get)
    assert updated_dt_get > updated_dt_orig, (
        f"'updated' timestamp after update is not newer than original. original={updated_dt_orig.isoformat()}, after_get={updated_dt_get.isoformat()}"
    )

    # Final sanity checks on returned article fields
    assert article_after_get.get("title") == "Updated Timestamp Article", "GET response title does not reflect updated title"
    assert article_after_get.get("slug") == slug, "GET response slug does not match original slug"

import requests
import pytest

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"


def create_user(email: str, password: str, full_name: str):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/signup"
    payload = {"email": email, "password": password, "full_name": full_name}
    r = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
    return r


def login_user(email: str, password: str):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/login/access-token"
    data = {"username": email, "password": password}
    r = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=10)
    return r


def get_auth_header(access_token: str):
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"}


def is_valid_uuid(val: str) -> bool:
    try:
        uuid.UUID(val)
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def assert_user_public_structure(obj: dict, expected_email: str):
    assert isinstance(obj, dict), "user response must be a JSON object"
    assert "email" in obj, "user object must contain 'email'"
    assert "id" in obj, "user object must contain 'id'"
    assert obj["email"] == expected_email, f"expected email {expected_email}, got {obj['email']}"
    assert isinstance(obj["id"], str) and is_valid_uuid(obj["id"]), "'id' must be a valid UUID string"


def assert_token_structure(obj: dict):
    assert isinstance(obj, dict), "token response must be a JSON object"
    assert "access_token" in obj, "token response must contain 'access_token'"
    assert isinstance(obj["access_token"], str) and len(obj["access_token"]) > 0, "'access_token' must be a non-empty string"
    # token_type may be present and typically is 'bearer'
    assert "token_type" in obj, "token response must contain 'token_type'"
    assert isinstance(obj["token_type"], str) and obj["token_type"].lower() == "bearer", "token_type must be 'bearer'"


def test_user_cannot_delete_another_user():
    # Generate unique test credentials
    unique = uuid.uuid4().hex
    user_a_email = f"test_a_{unique}@example.com"
    user_b_email = f"test_b_{unique}@example.com"
    password_a = "strongpasswordA1"
    password_b = "strongpasswordB1"
    full_name_a = "Test A"
    full_name_b = "Test B"

    # Create User A
    r = create_user(user_a_email, password_a, full_name_a)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"expected 200 creating user A, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    user_a = r.json()
    assert_user_public_structure(user_a, user_a_email)
    user_a_id = user_a["id"]

    # Create User B
    r = create_user(user_b_email, password_b, full_name_b)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"expected 200 creating user B, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    user_b = r.json()
    assert_user_public_structure(user_b, user_b_email)
    user_b_id = user_b["id"]

    # Login as User A to get access token
    r = login_user(user_a_email, password_a)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"expected 200 logging in as user A, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    token_resp_a = r.json()
    assert_token_structure(token_resp_a)
    token_a = token_resp_a["access_token"]

    # Attempt to delete User B using User A's token
    delete_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/{user_b_id}"
    headers = get_auth_header(token_a)
    r = requests.delete(delete_url, headers=headers, timeout=10)

    # The expected strict behavior: a user must NOT be able to delete another user -> Forbidden (403)
    assert r.status_code == 403, (
        f"expected 403 Forbidden when user A attempts to delete user B, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    )

    # Verify response is JSON and contains a 'detail' field describing the error
    assert r.headers.get("Content-Type", "").startswith("application/json"), "response must be JSON"
    err_json = r.json()
    assert isinstance(err_json, dict), "error response must be a JSON object"
    assert "detail" in err_json, "error response must contain 'detail' key"
    assert isinstance(err_json["detail"], str) and len(err_json["detail"]) > 0, "'detail' must be a non-empty string"

    # Finally, verify User B still exists by logging in as User B (proves not deleted)
    r = login_user(user_b_email, password_b)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"expected 200 logging in as user B after failed deletion, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    token_resp_b = r.json()
    assert_token_structure(token_resp_b)
    # Sanity: ensure token for user B is different from user A token (very likely)
    assert token_resp_b["access_token"] != token_a, "access tokens for different users should not be identical"

    user_data = resp.json()

    assert "token" in user_resp
    assert "username" in user_resp
    token = user_resp["token"]
    username_from_resp = user_resp["username"]
    assert username_from_resp == username

    # Use token to get user ID via PUT /user (since GET doesn't return ID)
    # We need to send at least one field; we'll send bio empty string.
    update_url = f"{base_url}/user"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Token {token}"}
    update_payload = {
        "user": {
            "bio": ""
        }
    }
    resp = requests.put(update_url, headers=headers, json=update_payload)

    payload_encoded = parts[1]
    # Add padding as needed
    padded = payload_encoded + '=' * (4 - len(payload_encoded) % 4)
    payload_decoded = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded)
    payload = json.loads(payload_decoded)

    # Assert token contains correct user ID and username
    # We expect claims "id" and "username" to be present.
    assert "id" in payload, "JWT payload missing 'id' claim"
    assert "username" in payload, "JWT payload missing 'username' claim"

def test_normal_user_cannot_create_another_user():
    """Verify a normal user cannot create another user."""
    base_url = "http://localhost:8000"
    
    # First, register a normal user
    normal_user_email = f"normaluser_{uuid.uuid4()}@example.com"
    normal_user_password = "testpassword123"
    
    register_response = requests.post(
        f"{base_url}/api/v1/users/signup",
        json={
            "email": normal_user_email,
            "password": normal_user_password,
            "full_name": "Normal User"
        }
    )
    assert register_response.status_code == 200
    
    # Login as the normal user to get access token
    login_response = requests.post(
        f"{base_url}/api/v1/login/access-token",
        data={
            "username": normal_user_email,
            "password": normal_user_password
        }
    )
    assert login_response.status_code == 200
    token_data = login_response.json()
    access_token = token_data["access_token"]
    
    # Verify the user is not a superuser
    me_response = requests.get(
        f"{base_url}/api/v1/users/me",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"}
    )
    assert me_response.status_code == 200
    user_data = me_response.json()
    assert user_data["is_superuser"] is False
    
    # Attempt to create another user using the normal user's token
    new_user_email = f"newuser_{uuid.uuid4()}@example.com"
    create_user_response = requests.post(
        f"{base_url}/api/v1/users/",

        },
    )

    token_json = token_resp.json()
    assert "access_token" in token_json, "Missing access_token in login response"
    access_token = token_json["access_token"]

    # 2. Create a new user (registered user) using admin credentials
    new_user_payload = {
        "email": "testuser@example.com",
        "password": "TestPass123",
        "full_name": "Test User",
    }
    create_resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/",
        json=new_user_payload,
        headers=auth_headers,
    )

    # Verify response structure and types

    assert isinstance(created_user["email"], str), "User email is not a string"
    assert created_user["email"] == new_user_payload["email"]

        "email": str,

        "is_superuser": bool,

    assert fetched_user["email"] == new_user_payload["email"], "Fetched email mismatch"
    # full_name may be returned as the value we set or null

import time
import requests

def test_unfollow_updates_profile_follow_status():
    base = "http://localhost:3000"
    api = f"{base}/api"

    # Helper functions for API interactions
    def register_user(username: str, email: str, password: str) -> str:
        url = f"{api}/users"
        payload = {"user": {"username": username, "email": email, "password": password}}
        resp = requests.post(url, json=payload)
        assert resp.status_code in (200, 201), f"Register failed with status {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(data, dict), "Register response is not a JSON object"
        assert "user" in data, "Register response missing 'user'"
        user = data["user"]
        assert isinstance(user, dict), "'user' in response is not an object"
        assert user.get("username") == username, "Registered username does not match"
        assert "token" in user and isinstance(user["token"], str) and user["token"], "Token missing in registered user"
        return user["token"]

    def get_profile(username: str, token: str = None) -> dict:
        url = f"{api}/profiles/{username}"
        headers = {}
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Token {token}"
        resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Get profile failed with status {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert "profile" in data, "Profile response missing 'profile'"
        profile = data["profile"]
        assert isinstance(profile, dict), "'profile' is not an object"
        assert profile.get("username") == username, "Profile username mismatch"
        assert "following" in profile, "Profile missing 'following' field"
        return profile

    def follow_user(username: str, token: str) -> dict:
        url = f"{api}/profiles/{username}/follow"
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Token {token}"}
        resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers)
        assert resp.status_code in (200, 201), f"Follow failed with status {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert "profile" in data, "Follow response missing 'profile'"
        profile = data["profile"]
        assert profile.get("username") == username, "Follow response profile username mismatch"
        assert "following" in profile, "Follow response missing 'following'"
        assert profile["following"] is True, "Profile should be following after follow"
        return profile

    def unfollow_user(username: str, token: str) -> dict:
        url = f"{api}/profiles/{username}/follow"
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Token {token}"}
        resp = requests.delete(url, headers=headers)
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Unfollow failed with status {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert "profile" in data, "Unfollow response missing 'profile'"
        profile = data["profile"]
        assert profile.get("username") == username, "Unfollow response profile username mismatch"
        assert "following" in profile, "Unfollow response missing 'following'"
        assert profile["following"] is False, "Profile should not be following after unfollow"
        return profile

    # Create two test users with unique usernames to avoid collisions
    timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
    user1 = f"unfollow_user1_{timestamp}"
    user2 = f"unfollow_user2_{timestamp}"
    email1 = f"{user1}@example.com"
    email2 = f"{user2}@example.com"
    password = "Password123!"

    # Register both users (token required for actions)
    token_user1 = register_user(user1, email1, password)
    token_user2 = register_user(user2, email2, password)  # Token not strictly needed for the test flow

    # Step 1: Ensure user1 views user2's profile with following = False initially
    profile_before = get_profile(user2, token_user1)
    assert profile_before["username"] == user2, "Initial profile username mismatch"
    assert "following" in profile_before, "Initial profile missing 'following' field"
    assert profile_before["following"] is False, "Initial following status should be False"

    # Step 2: user1 follows user2
    profile_after_follow = follow_user(user2, token_user1)
    assert profile_after_follow["username"] == user2, "Profile after follow username mismatch"
    assert profile_after_follow["following"] is True, "Following status should be True after follow"

    # Step 3: user1 unfollows user2
    profile_after_unfollow = unfollow_user(user2, token_user1)
    assert profile_after_unfollow["username"] == user2, "Profile after unfollow username mismatch"
    assert profile_after_unfollow["following"] is False, "Following status should be False after unfollow"

    # Step 4: Re-fetch profile to confirm status is updated in subsequent requests
    final_profile = get_profile(user2, token_user1)
    assert final_profile["username"] == user2, "Final profile username mismatch"
    assert "following" in final_profile, "Final profile missing 'following' field"
    assert final_profile["following"] is False, "Final following status should be False after unfollow"

import time
import requests
from datetime import datetime

def parse_datetime(dt_str):
    if not dt_str:
        return datetime.min
    s = dt_str
    if s.endswith("Z"):
        s = s[:-1] + "+00:00"
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(s)
    except Exception:
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z")
        except Exception:
            try:
                return datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
            except Exception:

LOGIN_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/login/access-token"
PASSWORD_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/me/password"


def _login(email: str, password: str) -> str:
    """Return access token for given credentials, asserting successful login."""
    resp = requests.post(
        LOGIN_URL,
        data={"username": email, "password": password},
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
    )

    # token_type is optional in spec defaulting to "bearer"
    if "token_type" in data:
        assert isinstance(data["token_type"], str), "token_type is not a string"
    return data["access_token"]


def _change_password(token: str, current_pw: str, new_pw: str) -> None:
    """Patch password endpoint and assert success."""
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    payload = {"current_password": current_pw, "new_password": new_pw}
    resp = requests.patch(PASSWORD_URL, json=payload, headers=headers)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Password change failed with status {resp.status_code}"

    # Base URLs

    mailcatcher_base_url = "http://localhost:1080"

        f"{api_base_url}/api/v1/password-recovery/{test_email}"
    )

def test_password_recovery_sends_email_to_recipient_and_mailcatcher_verifies():
    # Generate a unique test email to avoid clashes with existing users
    timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
    test_email = f"recover_test_{timestamp}@example.com"
    test_password = "TestPassword123"

    # 1) Register a new user for password recovery
    signup_resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/signup", json={
        "email": test_email,
        "password": test_password
    })
    assert signup_resp.status_code == 200, f"Signup failed with status {signup_resp.status_code}"
    signup_json = signup_resp.json()
    assert isinstance(signup_json, dict)
    assert "id" in signup_json, "Signup response missing 'id'"
    assert signup_json.get("email") == test_email, "Signup response email mismatch"

    # 2) Trigger password recovery for the new user
    recover_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/password-recovery/{test_email}"
    recover_resp = requests.post(recover_url)
    assert recover_resp.status_code == 200, f"Password recovery endpoint returned {recover_resp.status_code}"
    recover_json = recover_resp.json()
    assert isinstance(recover_json, dict)
    assert "message" in recover_json, "Password recovery response missing 'message'"
    assert isinstance(recover_json["message"], str) and len(recover_json["message"]) > 0, "Invalid recovery message"

    # 3) Verify that an email was sent to the recipient via mailcatcher
    max_wait_seconds = 20
    poll_interval = 1
    email_found = False
    message_id = None

    for _ in range(0, max_wait_seconds, poll_interval):
        try:
            mail_resp = requests.get(f"{MAILCATCHER_URL}/messages.json")
        except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
            mail_resp = None

        if mail_resp is not None and mail_resp.status_code == 200:
            try:
                messages = mail_resp.json()
            except ValueError:
                messages = []

            if isinstance(messages, list):
                for msg in messages:
                    if not isinstance(msg, dict):
                        continue
                    recipients = msg.get("recipients") or msg.get("to") or msg.get("To") or []
                    if isinstance(recipients, str):
                        recipients = [recipients]
                    if test_email in recipients:
                        email_found = True
                        message_id = msg.get("id")
                        break
            if email_found:
                break
        time.sleep(poll_interval)

    assert email_found, f"Password recovery email was not found in mailcatcher for recipient {test_email}"

    # 4) Optional: fetch email details to confirm recipient consistency
    if message_id is not None:
        detail_resp = requests.get(f"{MAILCATCHER_URL}/messages/{message_id}.json")
        if detail_resp.status_code == 200:
            try:
                detail = detail_resp.json()
                detail_recipients = detail.get("recipients") or detail.get("to") or detail.get("To") or []
                if isinstance(detail_recipients, str):
                    detail_recipients = [detail_recipients]

def _login(email: str, password: str) -> str:
    resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/login/access-token",

    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {resp.text}"

    assert isinstance(token, str) and token
    return token


def _get_current_user(token: str):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/users/me", headers=headers)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Get current user failed: {resp.text}"
    return resp.json()


def _create_item(token: str, title: str, description: str = None):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    payload = {"title": title}
    if description is not None:
        payload["description"] = description
    resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/items/", json=payload, headers=headers)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Create item failed: {resp.text}"
    data = resp.json()
    assert "id" in data and "owner_id" in data and "title" in data
    assert data["title"] == title
    return data


def _delete_item(token: str, item_id: str):

    return requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/items/{item_id}", headers=headers)

    user2_email = f"user2_{uuid.uuid4()}@example.com"

    # create two users
    user1_id = _signup(user1_email, pwd)
    user2_id = _signup(user2_email, pwd)

    u1 = body["user"]

    assert isinstance(u1.get("email"), str) and u1["email"] == user1["email"]
    assert isinstance(u1.get("token"), str) and len(u1["token"]) > 0
    token1 = u1["token"]

    # Create user2
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/users", json={"user": user2}, timeout=10)
    assert r.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201 Created for user2 creation, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict) and "user" in body, "Response must be a JSON object with 'user' key for user2 creation"

    assert isinstance(u2.get("email"), str) and u2["email"] == user2["email"]
    assert isinstance(u2.get("token"), str) and len(u2["token"]) > 0
    # token for user2 not needed further

    headers_user1 = {"Authorization": f"Token {token1}"}

    r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/profiles/{user2['username']}", headers=headers_user1, timeout=10)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 OK for GET profile before follow, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict) and "profile" in body, "GET profile response must contain 'profile'"
    profile = body["profile"]
    # Validate profile structure
    assert isinstance(profile.get("username"), str) and profile["username"] == user2["username"]
    assert "bio" in profile and isinstance(profile.get("bio"), (str, type(None)))  # bio may be None or string
    assert "image" in profile and isinstance(profile.get("image"), (str, type(None)))
    assert "following" in profile and isinstance(profile["following"], bool)
    assert profile["following"] is False, "Expected 'following' to be False when no relationship exists"

    # 2) user1 follows user2 via POST /profiles/{username}/follow
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/profiles/{user2['username']}/follow", headers=headers_user1, timeout=10)
    # Spec allows 200 or 201; the common behavior is 200. We assert 200 here strictly.
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 OK for follow request, got {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
